verdict.rationale: Sumsub's MCP server documentation says AI agents operate under the user's existing Sumsub role permissions. That gives agent access a role-based permission boundary, and the dashboard lets you assign roles to control access. However, the evidence does not show issuing dedicated, narrowly scoped API tokens or keys for an agent; app tokens are mentioned only in a sandbox context, with no description of scopes. Missing for 10: documented per-credential scopes or permissions for API or app tokens, a way to mint agent-specific least-privilege keys, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Use the MCP server to let AI agents perform Sumsub operations on your behalf, while keeping access controlled by your existing Sumsub role permissions.
you can invite any number of team members to the Sumsub Dashboard and control their access by assigning appropriate roles
